title: Paired Signal

story.briefing: Two transmitters somewhere in this unsorted capture combine to the resonant frequency. Unlike the conduit, nothing here arrives in order.
story.success: Resonant pair found. The forest canopy stops humming.

description: Given an array of frequencies in no particular order and a target, find two different positions whose values add up to the target. Return their indices as [i, j] with i less than j. If more than one pair works, return the one whose *second* index is smallest — that is, the pair that completes earliest as you scan left to right. Return an empty array if no pair works.

examples.explanation: 5 + 1 completes at index 1, earlier than any other pair.

hints: For each value you can compute exactly what its partner must be. The question is whether you have already seen that partner.
Sorting would destroy the indices you have to report. Remember values as you pass them instead.

Walk the array once, keeping a map from value to its earliest index. At each position, look up target minus the current value; if it is present, you have the earliest-completing pair. Otherwise record the current value and continue.
